feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader: the progression at NACo is clear, the scope is substantial, and the profile aligns well with strategy-heavy roles. Writing is polished overall, but the document is somewhat repetitive and overly dense in skills/sectioning, which slightly reduces impact and scanability.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression and credibility: multiple promotions at the same organization show growth, trust, and increasing leadership scope.  
- Good use of scale and specificity: “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and named tools/platforms add impact and believability.  
- Strong positioning for digital strategy roles: combines communications leadership, technical execution, analytics, and governance effectively.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT.” These sections overlap heavily; consolidating them would improve structure and readability.  
- Add more outcome-focused results beyond activity descriptions, especially in the freelance role and earlier NACo roles (e.g., engagement growth, efficiency gains, campaign performance).  
- Minor writing/style issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “12 years of experience”; punctuation in lists is slightly inconsistent (e.g., some comma/serial-list style varies); “French (A2/Learning)” reads awkwardly—prefer “French (A2, currently learning).”
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It would be sharper with a more distinctive opening, tighter phrasing, and a few specifics that reflect the most recent enterprise web and systems work.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner, standard phrasing.
- Lead with seniority and niche: digital strategy, platform modernization, and content operations for mission-driven/member organizations.
- Reduce generic lists (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”) and emphasize outcomes-oriented strengths like governance, workflows, and cross-functional execution.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience driving web, content, email, social, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel communications, platform modernization, and content operations, with a strong track record building the governance, workflows, and systems that support complex teams. Experienced in advocacy messaging, stakeholder alignment, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible communications.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications” and “stakeholder coordination” already appear in Core Competencies/Soft Skills; keep the intro higher-level.
- Avoid adding tool names or channel metrics here since those are covered well in Work Experience and skills sections.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant mix of strategic, technical, and operational strengths, but it overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. Tightening the phrasing and reducing generic items will make it feel sharper and more differentiated.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace broad phrases with more distinctive, senior-level language: “Enterprise digital strategy,” “CMS modernization,” “Editorial governance & workflow design,” “Analytics, KPI reporting & optimization.”
- Standardize style and parallel structure; use either all noun phrases or all “X & Y” constructions.
- Consider a tighter version: Enterprise digital strategy • CMS modernization & web operations • Editorial governance & workflow design • Multi-channel communications leadership • Analytics, KPI reporting & optimization • Cross-functional stakeholder coordination • Advocacy & policy communications • Multimedia, livestream & event production
- Change “communication” to “communications” for consistency with the rest of the CV.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital strategy,” “multi-channel communications,” “stakeholder coordination,” and “policy/advocacy communications” repeat the header almost verbatim.
- Several items also duplicate Topline Skills, especially web/CMS, analytics, and multimedia production.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope and technical depth, but it reads as a task list. Tighten it around outcomes, scale, and the most distinctive contributions so it complements—rather than repeats—your NACo leadership roles.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper positioning line: “Embedded strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvement, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets on systems/workflows/governance into one impact-led bullet: “Improved cross-channel communications operations by redesigning web workflows, analytics, and governance across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Make the Drupal/campaign work more outcome-oriented: mention number of microsites, campaigns, toolkits, publishers, traffic, or turnaround-time improvements if available.
- Rephrase the AI work as a flagship achievement: “Led an AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content preparation, and user-facing discovery experience.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” overlaps with the Director of Digital Media entry; keep this version more hands-on and consulting-specific.
- The Drupal microsite and AI search bullets may duplicate Recent Projects; keep the CV item high-level and let the footer hold examples.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize enterprise outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web modernization, analytics, governance, multimedia operations, and budget oversight across enterprise communications.”
- Combine and streamline channel language: replace the newsletter/social bullet with outcome-focused phrasing, e.g., “Oversaw NACo’s core digital channels—web, email, social, and video—serving county officials nationwide.”
- Strengthen results in key bullets: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal site serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable impact where possible for studio/analytics/governance bullets: cost savings, faster reporting, improved publishing consistency, reduced vendor reliance, increased production volume, or stronger campaign performance.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Newsletter/social/video execution overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- “Governance, publishing standards, and planning systems” overlaps with the header/core competencies, so make the operational outcome explicit.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry is too close to the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more clearly about executional leadership, channel ownership, and systems-building at this stage.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead line to emphasize scope and level: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial delivery and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Tighten bullets and start with actions/outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Clarify the video impact: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring channel for policy communications.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger systems bullet: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency and coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Led day-to-day digital communications operations” overlaps with the Director role’s channel oversight; use “managed” or “ran” to preserve progression.
- “Weekly video updates” also appears in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this entry as scaling/formalizing the program.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline skills item overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should be tighter, more distinctive, and framed around leadership scope rather than repeating generic capability labels.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to something sharper, e.g. **Digital Strategy, Governance & Communications Leadership**
- Replace generic phrases with higher-value wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy for high-volume public-sector platforms
- Editorial governance, publishing standards and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership across web, email, social and video
- Advocacy and mission-driven messaging strategy
- Audience-centered content planning and storytelling
- Keep to 4–5 bullets max and use parallel noun phrases.
- If space is tight, cut “audience-focused content planning,” which is the least differentiated.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” repeat the header/Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” also overlaps with Core Competencies’ “Advocacy and public-sector communications.”

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw keyword dump and overlaps heavily with the more detailed “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should be tighter, more strategic, and weighted toward recent strengths like Drupal, CMS modernization, integrations, automation, and AI search.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing: “Drupal & enterprise CMS platforms (WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages)”
- Replace “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” with a tighter phrase: “Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery)”
- Group related items to improve scanability: “CMS modernization • API integrations & workflow automation • Airtable systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Suggested rewrite: “Drupal & enterprise CMS platforms (WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages) • CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations & workflow automation • Airtable systems • AI-enabled search experiences”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills higher-level and let the technical section hold the full tool list.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” already appears in Core Competencies and the header summary.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. It also overlaps heavily with “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT, so this section should emphasize strategic application over software names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Analytics strategy & reporting” rather than just platform names.
- Tighten and group related items: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity” + “KPI framework design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis.”
- Consider this rewrite: “Analytics strategy & reporting • KPI framework design • Executive/leadership dashboards • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity • SEO and digital performance analysis”
- If space allows elsewhere, add measurable context tied to recent work, such as supporting a 10,000+ page site and 3.5M annual page views.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates the “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization” section almost exactly.
- “Leadership reporting” may be better aligned with executive dashboards/reporting to avoid vague repetition.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value capabilities tied to recent leadership work rather than listing basic production tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from task list to capability summary: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ and studio camera systems • In-house studio operations”
- Consider replacing “Video production and editing” with “Broadcast-quality video production” to better reflect the NACo studio build and leadership scope.
- Shorten “Hybrid and virtual event production” to “Hybrid event delivery” unless virtual-only events are a major differentiator.
- If space allows elsewhere, reserve tools like Premiere Pro for Technical + IT and keep this section focused on outcomes/capabilities.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” overlaps with Core Competencies (“Multimedia production and livestream operations”); use distinct phrasing or remove one.
- PTZ/studio details may be too granular for Topline Skills if Technical + IT already covers multimedia tools.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This item should either be tightened to emphasize strongest/recent platforms or add light proficiency context.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize recent, high-value platforms first: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add level/context instead of just names: **Drupal (enterprise/public-sector) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Consider renaming the heading to sharpen scope: **CMS & Web Platform Administration**
- If Drupal is the clear differentiator, lead with it and consider dropping GitHub Pages if it’s not materially relevant to target roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider removing one version or using this section for tools only and Topline Skills for broader capabilities.
- “CMS modernization” already appears elsewhere, so don’t repeat that phrase here unless tied to a specific platform.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools actually used in recent roles and group items more clearly.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery”
- Add a second phrase for delivery/integration: “Technical integration & deployment: API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless used consistently elsewhere; “HTML, CSS, JavaScript” is cleaner.
- If accurate, add one outcome-oriented qualifier in a nearby summary, e.g., “used to support Drupal microsites, analytics tagging, and workflow automation for high-traffic public-sector sites.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Workflow automation” appears elsewhere; avoid repeating GitHub Actions/automation themes across multiple skills sections unless this section is the only technical detail list.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as an undifferentiated software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” elsewhere. Make it more strategic by grouping tools by use and emphasizing the platforms most tied to recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe by function, not just brand names: “Workflow automation & work management: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp.”
- Move collaboration tools out unless they are core system platforms; Slack, Teams are usually too generic for a technical skills line.
- Prioritize strongest/recently relevant tools first: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier, then project systems.
- If space allows, add light context for impact: “used to build editorial workflows, approvals, reporting automations and cross-team planning systems.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; consider trimming one side to avoid repetition.
- Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp all signal project management—listing all four may feel redundant unless each was materially used.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too bare relative to the rest of the CV. Since email leadership already appears in recent NACo roles, this should stay tool-focused and avoid restating channel ownership.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Replace with: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope qualifiers instead of generic tools: **enterprise email automation**, **member communications**, **newsletter operations**, or **journey-based campaigns**
- If one platform was primary in the 2022–2024 director role, list that first to reflect recency and strongest relevance

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding phrases like “managed newsletters” or “led email strategy” here; those are already covered in Work Experience
- “Engagement” may overlap with broader communications claims elsewhere; keep this entry platform-specific unless you can name a distinct CRM/member-engagement function

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression story, but this entry is too broad and overlaps with the stronger 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it more foundational: team-building, early platform/content execution, and light people support.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize progression and first-team build: “Promoted across two digital roles while helping establish NACo’s first in-house digital media function.”
- Tighten scope and remove generic phrasing: “Improved day-to-day workflows across web, email, social and multimedia production.”
- Add concrete outputs if available: website refresh scale, number/frequency of livestreams or weekly videos, audience growth, production volume, or engagement gains.
- Clarify supervision modestly: “Provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate” or “mentored,” unless it was formal management.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this item focused on launching/producing the format, not expanding it.
- “Strengthening workflows” repeats later governance/operations themes; frame this as early process-building rather than enterprise leadership.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generically and overlaps with later NACo roles in digital/multimedia. Emphasize the podcast launch and frame the rest as innovation/program support to preserve progression.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the clearest achievement: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production.”
- Tighten the first sentence and make it more specific: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county-focused programs and policy priorities.”
- Combine supporting duties into one concise clause: “Produced digital and multimedia content to support program communications and member engagement.”
- If possible, add scope or output metrics: number of episodes launched, audiences reached, projects coordinated, or teams/stakeholders supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid broad “digital content production” language that repeats later NACo entries focused on web, video, and digital operations.
- Don’t overstate leadership here; save team-building, channel ownership, and operational scale for the more recent NACo roles.
